properties.natural_language: The DAO fork irregular state change MUST only be triggered at exactly block number 1,920,000 on mainnet.
The total ether supply must be conserved during the DAO fork state change: the sum of balances transferred from DAO accounts must equal the increase in the recovery contract balance.
After the DAO fork state change completes, all 119 accounts in List L must have exactly zero ether balance.
List L must be a fixed, immutable set of exactly 115 child DAO contracts plus 4 principal accounts; it must never be modified at runtime.
For blocks in range 1,920,000-1,920,009, the extraData field MUST contain the hex-encoded string 'dao-hard-fork'; blocks without it must be rejected.
After block validation, a block with invalid extraData during the fork range must be in STATE-BLOCK-REJECTED and must not be applied to the chain.
A caller of the WithdrawDAO contract's withdraw() function must have a non-zero DAO token balance as verified by the mainDAO contract.
After a successful withdrawal, the caller must receive ether proportional to their DAO token balance; a failed transfer must throw an exception with no state changes.
The EIP-779 fork logic must only apply to the mainnet chain that followed the fork; clients on minority chains must not implement this state change.
The TransactionType byte in a received typed transaction must be in the range 0x00-0x7f (unsigned 8-bit, non-RLP range).
When a received transaction has an unknown TransactionType, the node SHOULD disconnect the sending peer.
When a received transaction has a known type but invalid payload, the node SHOULD disconnect the sending peer.
A new TransactionType MUST NOT be sent to peers until the fork activation block for that type has been reached.
TransactionType values must be globally unique and assigned coordinately through the EIP process to avoid collisions across networks.
Processing unknown transaction types must not crash or freeze the node; rejection and disconnect must complete before any resource exhaustion.
After fork activation, the node MAY send the new TransactionType to peers; before activation, it MUST NOT.
A block containing any unknown transaction type must be rejected entirely; partial processing of a block with mixed known/unknown types must not occur.
Nodes must not relay transactions with unknown TransactionTypes; relay must only occur for known, validated types.
An execution proof's prover_pubkey must belong to an active validator in the current beacon state before signature verification proceeds.
The BLS signature on a SignedExecutionProof must be valid under DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF (0x0D000000) using the prover's public key.
The execution proof data must pass cryptographic verification via proof_engine.verify_execution_proof before being accepted.
Both ExecutionEngine and ProofEngine must agree (AND logic) for an execution payload to be accepted; disagreement must result in block rejection.
After dual validation passes, the execution payload header must be cached in the beacon state's latest_execution_payload_header.
Execution proof size must not exceed MAX_PROOF_SIZE (300 KiB) to prevent bandwidth/memory-based DoS.
Only validators in the whitelist (up to MAX_WHITELISTED_PROVERS = 256) may submit execution proofs.
An execution proof that fails at any verification stage (prover check, BLS signature, or proof data) must be in STATE-PROOF-REJECTED with no state changes applied.
A deposit request from the execution layer must have a valid BLS signature verified by is_valid_deposit_signature before being queued.
A pending deposit must not be processed until its slot has been finalized, as verified by the finality check.
After processing a deposit within the churn limit, the target validator's balance must increase by the deposit amount, respecting max effective balance caps.
At most MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH (16) deposits may be processed per epoch; excess deposits must remain in the pending queue.
The execution layer must enforce MAX_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD (8192) before delivering deposit requests to the consensus layer.
A consolidation request must have source_address matching withdrawal credentials, both validators active, source != target, and neither slashed.
After a same-validator consolidation, the withdrawal_credentials prefix must change from 0x01 to 0x02, and excess balance above MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE must be queued as a pending deposit.
After a cross-validator consolidation completes, the source validator's balance must be zero and the target validator's balance must increase by min(source_balance, source_effective_balance).
Consolidation requests targeting validators already in the exit queue must be silently dropped.
An attestation must have valid committee_bits covering indices within MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT before computing attesting indices.
The aggregate BLS signature on an attestation must be valid for all computed attesting validators before the attestation is accepted.
After slashing an attester, the penalty must be exactly effective_balance / MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ELECTRA (4096), and the whistleblower must receive a reward at the 1/4096 rate.
A slashed validator must remain in the slashed state; slashing must not be reversible.
A withdrawal request must have source_address matching the validator's 0x01 withdrawal credentials, and the validator must be active and not already exiting.
When withdrawal amount is FULL_EXIT_REQUEST_AMOUNT (0), the validator must be assigned an exit epoch computed with churn limits.
At most MAX_PENDING_PARTIALS_PER_WITHDRAWALS_SWEEP (8) partial withdrawals may be processed per block.
The three churn tracks (activation/exit, consolidation, and deposit) must be independently rate-limited; consuming capacity in one track must not affect the others.
The activation/exit churn limit must be capped at min(balance_churn_limit, 256 ETH) per epoch.
The deposit_requests_start_index marks a clean cutoff: deposits with index < start_index come from the Eth1 bridge, and deposits with index >= start_index come from the execution layer.
The recipient's ephemeral public key R, when accompanied by a signerPubKey, must have a valid ECDSA/Ed25519 signature that can be verified before encapsulation proceeds.
If a trustedPubKey is provided, the signerPubKey must be signed by the trustedPubKey, forming a valid trust chain.
All ephemeral keys used in the protocol must be generated using a cryptographically secure random number generator (CSRNG).
After the ECIES encapsulation step completes, the output must be the concatenation of the sender's ephemeral public key S and the AES-GCM ciphertext of the private key.
After protocol completion, all ephemeral keys (both sender's and recipient's) must be securely destroyed to achieve perfect forward secrecy.
The private key must never exist in plaintext outside of sender and recipient application memory boundaries; during transport it must always be encrypted.
After successful decryption (intake), the recipient must have recovered the exact private key that the sender encapsulated.
The ECDH shared secret must be derived from the sender's ephemeral private key and the recipient's ephemeral public key; any mismatch makes decryption impossible.
If signature verification fails for the recipient's public key, the encapsulation protocol must abort with no key material transmitted.
The secp256k1-AES-128-GCM configuration must be supported as the mandatory baseline by all implementations.
Even resource-constrained sender devices must be capable of ECDSA/Ed25519 signature verification to validate recipient public keys.
SSZ chunks provided for progressive merkleization must be well-formed 32-byte chunks from a valid SSZ serialization.
For an empty input (len(chunks) == 0), the merkleization must return the zero hash Bytes32().
The generalized index for any element at a given position must be stable and capacity-independent; it must not change when the list grows.
The progressive tree structure must provide equivalent collision resistance and security properties to fixed-capacity merkle trees.
After merkleization, the final hash_tree_root must include a mix_in_length step that combines the merkle root with the list length.
A merkle proof request must specify a valid element index and list root before proof generation begins.
A completed merkle proof must contain all sibling hashes needed for verification and be verifiable against the list root.
Implementations must enforce context-specific bounds on list sizes rather than relying on the theoretical ~4GB uint32 limit.
The progressive subtree splitting pattern must follow 4^n scaling (1, 4, 16, 64...) for leaf counts at each level.
The caller must provide sufficient gas for the identity precompile: GAS_IDENTITY (15) base + GAS_IDENTITY_WORD (3) * ceil32(len(data))/32.
After the identity precompile executes, evm.output must contain an exact byte-for-byte copy of evm.message.data with no modification.
The identity precompile must be always available at address 0x04 and must accept any input data including empty input (0 bytes).
Input data size to the identity precompile is bounded only by available gas; there is no explicit size limit enforced.
If the caller has insufficient gas for the identity precompile, the operation must fail with an out-of-gas error and no output is produced.
Before any gas charge, evm.gas_left must be >= the amount to deduct; otherwise OutOfGasError must be raised.
After a successful gas charge, evm.gas_left must be reduced by exactly the charged amount.
evm.gas_left must never go negative; the gas check must always occur before deduction.
Memory expansion cost must follow the quadratic formula: linear_cost + quadratic_cost where quadratic_cost = size_in_words^2 / 512.
Blob gas must be entirely separate from execution gas, with its own pricing and limits per EIP-4844.
The blob base fee must always be >= MIN_BLOB_GASPRICE (1 wei); it must never be zero.
All nodes must compute the blob base fee identically using the same Taylor exponential approximation with BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION (3,338,477).
The 63/64 gas reservation rule must apply to all CALL, DELEGATECALL, and STATICCALL operations; the caller must retain at least 1/64th of remaining gas.
After a CALL with value > 0, the gas cost must include GAS_CALL_VALUE (9,000) and a GAS_CALL_STIPEND (2,300) must be provided to the child context.
After a CALL to a new (non-existent) account, an additional GAS_NEW_ACCOUNT (25,000) cost must be charged.
A cold SLOAD must charge GAS_COLD_SLOAD (2,100 gas) and then mark the slot as warm; subsequent accesses must charge only GAS_WARM_ACCESS (100 gas).
A storage write from zero to non-zero must charge GAS_STORAGE_SET (20,000 gas); a non-zero to zero write must add GAS_STORAGE_CLEAR_REFUND (4,800) to the refund counter.
Integer arithmetic for all gas calculations must not overflow within the bounds of valid transactions.
A received block must pass header validation (gas metrics, difficulty, parent constraints) before any further processing.
Ommer blocks must be validated: max 2 per block, no duplicates, age 1-6 blocks, valid parent, and not in canonical chain.
After applying the block body, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must all match the header values.
Before execution, a transaction must pass: gas available in block, valid signature recoverable to EOA, nonce match, and balance >= gas*price + value.
After extracting an access list, all specified addresses and storage keys must be marked as warm before transaction execution begins.
Gas refund from storage clears must be capped at 50% of gas consumed in the transaction.
After transaction execution, gas_used * gas_price must be transferred to the coinbase address.
Proof-of-work validation must verify the Ethash result: mix digest must match and result hash must meet the difficulty target.
Difficulty calculation must subtract BOMB_DELAY_BLOCKS (9,000,000) from the block number before computing the difficulty bomb component.
Duplicate addresses or storage keys in an access list must be deduplicated; each address/slot is marked warm only once.
Cold account access must cost 2600 gas, cold slot access 2100 gas, and warm access 100 gas per EIP-2929.
After a cold access, the accessed address/slot must be marked warm for all subsequent accesses within the same transaction.
Block reward must be exactly 2 ETH plus ommer bonuses, distributed to the coinbase address.
Access list gas costs must accurately reflect the true cost of storage operations, preventing economic DoS attacks through mispriced operations.
Access lists must not be weaponizable for disproportionate state bloat or processing cost relative to gas paid.
